subject: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?

messages.author: 0ac478a72563a365
messages.subject: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
parts:
I've ran into a problem installing R packages from private repositories on github. "github" source requires a password, which I don't want committed in the source code (that's a huge security hole). The closest I got to was to use a submodule and use local install. However, the lockfile contains the full path to the the source location which isn't very portable:

SourcePath:
  /Users/syrnick/xxxxx/vendor/rlibs/xyz-utils

It then fails to find the source of the package upon restore.

I also have to explicitly pass the location of the source explicitly to packrat::snapshot, but that's a minor nuisance. I just have a helper function that's goes over all private packages.

How do you deal with private repos?

Thanks!
Alex

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
parts: You're doing it the way we intended. The surprising thing is "it then fails to find the source of the package upon restore". When you're restoring, is there anything in ./packrat.sources/<packagename>? That's where packrat is supposed to go looking for it first, and we expect you to check the whole packrat.sources directory into source control.

messages.author: 0ac478a72563a365
messages.subject: Re: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
parts:
Thanks Joe!

The file is there. After running:

packrat::snapshot( sourcePackagePaths= c('./vendor/rlibs/xxxxx-utils'))      

Fetching sources for xxxxx.utils (0.0.2) ... OK (local) 

I get:

packrat.sources/xxxxxx.utils/xxxxx.utils_0.0.2.tar.gz , but it's size is only 29 bytes. It appears to be only null values (1024 of them) in the tar itself.

Actually, after digging around more, I realized that it works if I rename the path to match the source and it created the correct tgz file. 

Two issues still:
1) Ideally, I wouldn't even have that in sources, because it's already a submodule in the project.
2) the lock file has the full path to the submodule location (/Users/yyyy/zzzz/vendor/rlibs/xxxx.utils), which is specific to my machine and definitely not portable.

Alex
